applicability.defect: non-manifold geometry or a no-op modifier caused by incorrect stack order

preconditions: a modifier stack combines Mirror with Subdivision Surface, or Solidify with Bevel, or Boolean with Bevel, or Mirror with Bevel
the mesh has an open boundary that Mirror welds (Mirror+Subdivision, Mirror+Bevel), or is a flat/open shell that Solidify gives thickness to (Solidify+Bevel)
required_observations: evaluated vertex positions near the mirror seam, to distinguish a genuinely flat/continuous seam from a carved/rounded one
evaluated vertex/face count, to detect a modifier silently doing nothing (e.g. Bevel on an unsolidified plane)
action_policy: For Mirror plus Subdivision Surface, test both candidate orders on the actual seam topology. Subdivision-before-Mirror repaired the original flat-seam failure, but a later exact-seam half-cylinder stayed manifold in both orders; do not promote one shape's result into a universal order rule.

Bevel should be placed BEFORE Mirror when a seamless join across the mirror plane is wanted. Mirror-before-Bevel causes Bevel to treat the former seam edges as ordinary edges and round/carve them, producing a visible facet at what should be a flat, continuous seam.

Solidify must be placed BEFORE Bevel when starting from an open/flat mesh (e.g. a plane). Bevel on an unsolidified single-face plane has no dihedral angle to act on and is effectively a no-op; Solidify must run first to give the mesh real 3D form.

Boolean before or after Bevel is a genuine strategic choice, not a correctness issue: Boolean-then-Bevel rounds the cut/hole rim too (more geometry); Bevel-then-Boolean leaves the cut sharp (less geometry). Choose based on whether the cut's edge should read as rounded or crisp.

For Bevel plus Subdivision Surface, choose by edge function rather than a universal stack order: Bevel->Subdivision makes a broad physical radius part of the smoothed form; crease/support protection plus Subdivision->Bevel adds a tighter final chamfer to an already controlled form. Never use an unprotected post-Subdivision weighted Bevel when the base design line must stay fixed, and inspect three-edge corners for concentrated highlights in the crease-protected path.
expected_effects: Mirror+Subdivision: the selected order must have 0 non-manifold edges in the evaluated mesh and acceptable seam shape/highlight flow; topology-specific testing decides the order
Mirror+Bevel in the correct order (Bevel first): a flat, unrounded seam face at the mirror plane, with the two halves reading as one continuous surface
Solidify+Bevel in the correct order (Solidify first): the evaluated mesh's vertex/face count reflects real bevel geometry, not an unchanged flat shell
Bevel+Subdivision: the chosen order's radius, panel planarity, corner highlight concentration, and evaluated cost match the reference-defined edge function
success_predicates: no evaluated vertices with visibly rounded/offset coordinates sitting exactly on the mirror plane when a flat seam was intended
failure_predicates: evaluated_mesh_health.non_manifold_edges > 0 after evaluating either tested Mirror/Subdivision order on the actual seam topology
Bevel modifier added but the evaluated mesh's vertex/face count is unchanged from before adding it (Bevel silently doing nothing, usually because it ran before Solidify on a flat shell)
Post-Subdivision Bevel visibly rounds or relocates a design line that was not protected by crease/support topology, or creates concentrated corner highlights that contradict the reference
recovery: reorder the modifier stack (Blender modifiers can be reordered without data loss -- this does not require rebuilding geometry) and re-check non_manifold_edges / vertex-face counts on the evaluated mesh

sources.description: This project's own live reproduction, session 2026-08-07 (knowledge-first foundation phase): built matched pairs of scratch objects (a cube with its inner face touching a mirror plane; a plane for Solidify+Bevel) with modifiers added in both orders, compared via evaluated_probe-style inspection (vertex/face/non-manifold counts, seam vertex positions).
sources.trust_tier: not applicable (first-party direct experiment, not an external source)

experiments.type: controlled, matched-pair (this project's own reproduction lab, not an external tutorial)
experiments.description: Mirror+Subdivision: Mirror->Subdivision gave 171v/176f/16 non-manifold edges; Subdivision->Mirror gave 196v/192f/0 non-manifold edges, with the evaluated seam empty of exactly-on-plane vertices in the working order and populated with rounded-looking coordinates in the broken order. Mirror+Bevel: Mirror->Bevel gave 68v/67f/12 non-manifold with bevelled coordinates at the seam; Bevel->Mirror gave 108v/107f/4 non-manifold with a flat unbevelled seam face. Solidify+Bevel: Solidify->Bevel gave 56v/54f; Bevel->Solidify gave 8v/6f, identical to an un-bevelled solidified plane (confirming the no-op). Boolean+Bevel: both orders gave 0 non-manifold edges but different face counts (248v/216f vs 120v/88f), confirming this pair is a style choice, not a correctness issue.
experiments.limitation: Tested on simple primitive shapes (cube, plane, cube+cylinder cutter), not yet on a real production prop combining these modifiers. The original Mirror+Subdivision result was topology-specific and must be read alongside the curved transfer experiment.

experiments.description: On an exact-seam half-cylinder in runs/2026-08-10_bevel-mirror-transfer/, Mirror->Subdivision and Subdivision->Mirror both evaluated to 482 vertices, 480 quad faces, and 0 non-manifold edges. The intentionally offset Mirror seam produced 12 non-manifold edges and a larger Merge Distance repaired it. Independent evaluation of the saved blend reproduced all outcomes.
experiments.limitation: Manifoldness and counts do not prove identical curvature or highlight flow. The two stack orders had slightly different signed volumes, and neither was judged with a controlled reflection render.

experiments.type: controlled matched-cage visual and evaluated-surface comparison
experiments.description: Blender 5.2 comparison in runs/2026-08-15_bevel-subd-order/ used identical supported all-quad box cages and the same 36 semantic design-edge segments. Bevel->Subdivision produced 2,400 evaluated quads, 0 localized pinch candidates, and a broad continuous MatCap highlight. Crease(0.75)+Subdivision->Bevel produced 1,176 quads and the flattest panels but 16 concentrated corner-curvature candidates. Unprotected Subdivision->Bevel had the same count and bounds as the protected variant yet visibly over-rounded the form, disproving count-only comparison. A fresh process independently verified modifier order, crease placement, topology health, and render dimensions.
experiments.limitation: One supported rectangular box fixture; not transfer validation on a curved hull or production prop. The surface diagnostic reports candidates, not certain defects, and was interpreted alongside fixed-frame MatCap and evaluated-wire renders.

status_note: Controlled matched-pair evidence exists for the original four modifier pairs, a cylindrical second-shape transfer for Mirror+Subdivision, and fixed-frame MatCap/evaluated-wire evidence for Bevel versus Subdivision order. The evidence rejects universal ordering and requires per-topology, reference-defined evaluation. Not yet RUNTIME_VALIDATED or BENCHMARK_SUPPORTED; Bevel/Subdivision still needs curved-hull or real-prop transfer.
